title: Table views that stay correct
subtitle: Build a task list with stable identity, reusable cells, and predictable updates.
objectives: Explain the separate responsibilities of a table view, its data source, and its delegate.
Build self-sizing cells whose content is fully reset on every configuration.
Apply diffable snapshots using stable model identifiers.
Implement selection, refresh, deletion, and empty states without desynchronizing the model.
prerequisites: Days 3–7: UIKit lifecycle, Auto Layout, navigation, and reusable views.
Swift structs, UUID, dictionaries, and closures.

sections.title: 1. A table is a viewport over your model
body: UITableView is useful when people need to scan a vertical sequence: inbox messages, settings, search results, or PocketTasks items. The table creates only the cells needed for the visible region, with a small reuse buffer. Your model therefore cannot live in cells. Scrolling a row offscreen may recycle its cell for an entirely different task.

A data source answers which sections and rows exist and how each row should look. A delegate handles interactions and presentation decisions such as selection, swipe actions, and row sizing. With a diffable data source, you still use a delegate. Do not also implement the classic numberOfRowsInSection and cellForRowAt methods as a second competing source of truth.

sections.title: 2. Identity is different from position and content
body: An index path is the current location of a row, not the identity of a task. Inserting a new task at the top moves every later index path. Give each model a stable UUID and put those identifiers in the snapshot. Keep the actual models in a dictionary or repository keyed by UUID. Resolve the selected identifier through the data source when a user taps a row.

The snapshot describes ordered section and item identifiers at one moment. Applying it lets UIKit calculate insertions, moves, and removals. Changing a title in your dictionary does not automatically update an existing cell because the identifier has not changed. Use snapshot.reconfigureItems for content changes to existing identifiers. Create a new snapshot for membership or ordering changes.

sections.title: 3. Reuse requires complete configuration
body: Every cell configuration must set every visible state that varies: title, subtitle, image, accessory, color, and loading placeholder. A common bug sets a checkmark only when a task is complete; an incomplete task then inherits the checkmark from the previous occupant of the cell. Assign both branches explicitly. UIListContentConfiguration is a convenient starting point for standard cells.

Custom cells should create their subviews once in init and constrain them to contentView. Make a complete vertical constraint chain from the content view's top to bottom. Set a multiline label's numberOfLines to zero, use automaticDimension, and supply a reasonable estimatedRowHeight. prepareForReuse is useful for cancelling work and resetting transient state; it does not replace correct model configuration.

sections.title: 4. Mutation should flow through the model
body: For a swipe-to-delete action, resolve the item's current identifier, remove that identifier from your model, and then apply a snapshot representing the new model. Do not merely remove a row visually while leaving the record in storage: it will reappear on the next refresh. If deletion is remote, decide whether to wait for success or perform an optimistic deletion with a visible recovery path.

Selection should also resolve an identifier before navigating to details. Refresh controls should finish in both success and failure paths. An empty list deserves an explanatory background view and a useful action, while a failed request deserves a retry state. Those are distinct meanings even though both may currently display zero rows.

sections.title: 5. Keep scrolling work small and observable
body: Cell configuration runs frequently on the main actor. It should apply already-prepared presentation values, not perform networking, synchronously decode large images, or calculate expensive attributed strings. Prefetching can start upcoming work, but it is a performance hint rather than a guarantee. A row must still behave correctly when it appears without a prefetch callback.

When diagnosing a list bug, first inspect model identity and snapshot contents. Duplicate identifiers are invalid. For disappearing accessories, inspect complete configuration. For height problems, inspect constraints inside contentView. For stutter, profile on a device using Time Profiler rather than assuming the number of Swift lines determines performance.

example.title: A complete diffable task list
walkthrough: In an iOS UIKit app, add this file and make UINavigationController(rootViewController: TasksViewController(style: .insetGrouped)) the window's root controller in your existing scene setup. This is an app view controller, not a command-line Swift script.
The order array controls presentation order while the dictionary stores current model values. Each UUID is generated once when its model is created.
The cell provider captures the controller weakly because the controller owns the data source, which retains the provider closure.
Both accessory branches and both subtitle branches are assigned on every configuration, preventing recycled visual state.
Tapping resolves the UUID through the data source, updates the model, and reconfigures that same stable identifier.
example.expectedOutput: Three task rows appear. Long titles wrap and grow the row. Tapping any row toggles its subtitle and checkmark without creating a new task.

exercises.title: Repair a reused checkmark
exercises.prompt: A teammate's cell configuration only adds a checkmark for completed tasks. Rewrite it so unfinished tasks can never inherit old content, and explain why scrolling reveals the bug.
requirements: Set the title for both complete and incomplete tasks.
Use the TaskItem model from the example.
hints: The same cell object can represent several different models.
Each varying property needs a value for every model state.
exercises.explanation: Reuse preserves object properties. A one-sided conditional leaves the previous task's accessory untouched when the new task is incomplete. Full configuration makes the cell a rendering of the current model rather than a memory of past models.
checks: Configure one cell with a completed task, then an incomplete task; the checkmark disappears.
Repeat in the opposite order and verify both titles and subtitles.

exercises.title: Add tasks without changing existing identities
exercises.prompt: Extend TasksViewController with an addTask(title:) method. Insert the new task at the top and update the list without rebuilding UUIDs for existing tasks.
requirements: Trim leading and trailing whitespace and reject blank input.
Keep existing tasks and their completion state.
hints: Both order and tasks need updates before applying a snapshot.
exercises.explanation: Stable identifiers allow the diffable data source to recognize existing rows. Recreating every model with a fresh UUID would describe a replacement of the entire list and could lose selection or associated state. Call the method from a button or a temporary line after the initial snapshot.
checks: Add two tasks and confirm that they appear newest first.
Complete an existing task, add another, and verify that completion remains.
Pass only spaces and verify that the row count does not change.

exercises.title: Delete by identifier and render an empty state
exercises.prompt: Add a model-driven delete method and an empty-list message. Call the method from a temporary button or debug action before connecting a trailing swipe action.
requirements: Remove the identifier from both model containers.
Use a background view for the empty state.
Do not call deleteRows alongside a diffable snapshot.
hints: A background view belongs to the table rather than to a reusable cell.
Call updateEmptyState after every membership change.
exercises.explanation: One state transition updates the model and asks the snapshot to represent it. Mixing manual row deletion with diffable updates introduces a second, potentially contradictory update mechanism. Also call updateEmptyState after the initial load and addTask so the message always follows the model.
checks: Delete the first, middle, and last remaining task without an invalid-update crash.
After deleting all tasks, verify the message is visible.
Add a task and verify the message disappears.

quiz.question: What is the safest identity to store in a diffable snapshot for editable tasks?
options: The task's current row number
A stable UUID created with the task
The title, because it is visible
A new UUID every time the screen renders
quiz.explanation: Position and title can change. A stable identifier lets UIKit distinguish an existing item's changed content from an insertion or removal.

quiz.question: A task title changes, but its UUID stays the same. What should update the visible row?
options: Only change the dictionary and do nothing else
Remove the table from its superview
Update the model and reconfigure the existing identifier
Change every UUID
quiz.explanation: The snapshot's identifiers have not changed. Reconfiguration tells the cell provider to render current content for that existing item.

quiz.question: Why should custom cell constraints reference contentView?
options: It makes every cell the same height
UITableView ignores subviews outside it
It is the intended container and participates in cell layout and self-sizing
It prevents networking requests
quiz.explanation: The content view is UIKit's supported container for a cell's primary custom content. Correct edge-to-edge vertical constraints enable fitting-size calculation.

quiz.question: Where should a completed task's persistent state live?
options: Only in the cell's accessoryType
In the model or repository
Only in prepareForReuse
In the current index path
quiz.explanation: A cell is a temporary presentation object. Model state must survive scrolling, navigation, reordering, and reconstruction of views.

quiz.question: What does prefetching guarantee?
options: Every row is prefetched before display
A fixed number of requests
Nothing about correctness; it is an opportunity to prepare data early
That no cancellation logic is needed
quiz.explanation: Prefetch callbacks are hints. Display logic must still handle missing data, repeated requests, and work that becomes unnecessary.

pitfalls: Generating new item IDs whenever you apply a snapshot.
Capturing the controller strongly in a retained cell-provider closure.
Configuring only one branch of accessories, colors, or placeholders.
Combining manual insertRows/deleteRows with a diffable data source.
Performing synchronous network or image-decoding work during cell configuration.
checkpoint: Explain why an index path is not a stable model identifier.
Toggle and add tasks while preserving old UUIDs.
Show a long title without clipping at a larger text size.
Trace one reused cell through two different model configurations.
Describe how remote deletion would recover if the server rejects it.

capstone.title: PocketTasks milestone: the task inbox
steps: Replace static labels with the diffable task list.
Support creating, toggling, and removing tasks through stable identifiers.
Add an empty state and document which class owns the task models.
Manually test a long list, large text, and repeated add/delete operations.
